bull.b: The Anthropic lease provides substantial long-term revenue visibility and expands TeraWulf beyond bitcoin mining into AI infrastructure. A multi-decade contract with a major customer can support project financing, improve asset utilization, and create a durable base for capacity expansion.

Doubling Muskie’s contracted power capacity strengthens TeraWulf’s ability to develop a larger AI and high-performance computing campus. The expanded utility arrangement increases future capacity potential and advances the company’s strategy of building power-advantaged infrastructure at scale.

Rapid growth in HPC lease revenue indicates that TeraWulf is progressing from platform development toward recurring infrastructure revenue. A larger leasing contribution can make the business mix less dependent on bitcoin mining and improve revenue visibility as additional contracted capacity becomes operational.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating cash flow shows that the core business is not currently self-funding, while very large negative free cash flow reflects substantial funding needs. Continued burn can constrain flexibility and increase dependence on debt, asset sales, or other financing.

The combination of very high debt relative to equity and reported zero TTM equity indicates limited balance-sheet support for the company’s expansion plan. Heavy leverage can raise financing costs, reduce resilience to operating setbacks, and restrict future capital allocation flexibility.

Negative adjusted EBITDA and a large gap between current and targeted reported leasing margins show that new capacity is carrying meaningful pre-revenue and development costs. Until projects ramp, operating losses may continue to absorb cash and weaken near-term earnings quality.
